title: Integral closure with geometrically normal scalar extensions
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a finitely generated commutative $k$-algebra which is geometrically integral: $A\otimes_k L$ is an integral domain (a nonzero ring without zero divisors) for every field extension $L/k$. Let $F=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ and let $B\subset F$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $F$, consisting of the elements satisfying monic polynomials over $A$. Suppose $B$ is finite as an $A$-module and geometrically normal over $k$: every local ring of $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_k L)$ is an integrally closed domain for every field extension $L/k$. For every such $L$, the natural map $B\otimes_k L\to\operatorname{Frac}(A\otimes_k L)$ is injective and identifies its source with the integral closure of $A\otimes_k L$ in its fraction field. In particular $B\otimes_k L$ is an integrally closed domain, finite over $A\otimes_k L$. These identifications commute with homomorphisms of extension fields over $k$ and with principal localization $A\to A[1/f]$ for $0\ne f\in A$.

The field and algebra notions use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], [def-pc-scheme] and [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

proof.text: Fix $L/k$ and write $C=A\otimes_kL$, $D=B\otimes_kL$, $E=\operatorname{Frac}(C)$ and $S=A\setminus\{0\}$. The algebra tensor product has multiplication $(a\otimes\lambda)(a\prime\otimes\mu)=aa\prime\otimes\lambda\mu$. Since $L$ is flat over $k$, tensoring the inclusions $A\subset B\subset F$ gives inclusions $C\subset D\subset F\otimes_kL$. Localization over the first factor identifies $F\otimes_kL=S^{-1}C$: $(a/s)\otimes\lambda\mapsto(a\otimes\lambda)/(s\otimes1)$. The map $A\to C$ is injective: choose a $k$-linear functional $L\to k$ taking $1$ to $1$ and tensor it with $A$ to obtain a retraction. Thus each $s\otimes1$ is nonzero. As $C$ is a domain by hypothesis, $S^{-1}C\to E$, $c/s\mapsto c/s$, is injective by the fraction equivalence relation. Composing gives the required canonical injection $j_L:D\hookrightarrow E$.

source.place: Tag 0C3N (lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields), affine comparison; algebra Tags 00DK/00D2 for tensor localization

proof.text: Choose $A$-module generators $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ of $B$. If $b=\sum_i a_i b_i$, then $b\otimes\lambda=\sum_i(a_i\otimes\lambda)(b_i\otimes1)$. Since pure tensors generate $D$, the $b_i\otimes1$ generate it as a $C$-module. Hence $D$ is finite over $C$, and the finite-algebra integrality lemma says that every element of $D$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $C$. Applying $j_L$ to this equation shows that $j_L(D)$ is contained in the integral closure of $C$ in $E$.

The inclusions $C\subset D\subset E$ show that $D$ is a domain and its fraction field is $E$: every $c/c\prime\in E$, with $c,c\prime\in C$ and $c\prime\ne0$, is already a fraction of elements of $D$, while any fraction of elements of $D$ lies in $E$. For every prime $\mathfrak q\subset D$, the affine-stalk theorem identifies $D_{\mathfrak q}$ with $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}D,\mathfrak q}$. These local rings are integrally closed domains by the geometric normality hypothesis on $B$. Thus $D$ is a normal ring. The normal-ring total-fractions theorem applies, and, since $D$ is a domain and its total fraction ring is $E$, it is integrally closed in $E$.

proof.text: Let $x\in E$ be integral over $C$. Its monic equation over $C\subset D$ is also a monic equation over $D$. The integral closedness proved in Step 3 therefore gives $x\in j_L(D)$. Combined with Step 2 this proves equality with the integral closure, as subrings of the specified fraction field. The finiteness and domain assertions were established in Steps 2 and 3.

source.place: Tag 0C3N (lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields), equality of the normal tensor algebra with the integral closure

proof.text: For a $k$-homomorphism $u:L\to M$ of extension fields, $A\otimes_kL\to A\otimes_kM$ is injective: a linear retraction $M\to L$ of the inclusion $u(L)\subset M$, after identifying $L$ with its image, tensors to a retraction. Thus there is a map of fraction fields $E_L\to E_M$, $c/d\mapsto u_A(c)/u_A(d)$. Write an element $b\in B$ as $a/s\in F$. Then $j_L(b\otimes\lambda)=(a\otimes\lambda)/(s\otimes1)$. Both composites from $B\otimes_kL$ to $E_M$ send it to $(a\otimes u(\lambda))/(s\otimes1)$. Additivity and generation by pure tensors prove equality on all elements. Images of monic equations are monic equations, so the fraction-field map restricts to the integral closures. Since the identifications of Step 4 are these actual embeddings, this proves their naturality, including identities and composition.

source.place: Tag 0C3N (lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields), canonical affine maps; agent extension: explicit field-homomorphism square

proof.text: For $0\ne f\in A$, let $g=f\otimes1\in C$, which is nonzero by Step 1. Apply integral-closure localization first to $A\subset F$ and then to $C\subset E$. Since nonzero $f$ and $g$ are already units in the respective fields, it identifies the two localized integral closures as $B[1/f]\subset F$ and $D[1/g]\subset E$. Principal algebra localization under base change gives $A[1/f]\otimes_kL=C[1/g]$ and $B[1/f]\otimes_kL=D[1/g]$, with $(b/f^n)\otimes\lambda\mapsto(b\otimes\lambda)/g^n$. Under these maps the localized comparison sends this tensor to $j_L(b\otimes\lambda)/g^n$. This is also its image via the comparison constructed from $A[1/f]\subset F$. Thus the localization square commutes on pure tensors and hence everywhere. The same formula with $\lambda$ replaced by $u(\lambda)$ shows compatibility with field homomorphisms simultaneously. No assumption that localized $B$ is geometrically normal is needed for this comparison: its integral-closure description follows directly from the localization lemma.
